research_rationale:
Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 11085 (The Presidential Medal of Freedom, February 22, 1963, 28 FR 1759), read in full from the held Federal Register text after splitting the packet inventory (four mixed scopes) into twelve separately decided commands. The order is mostly an amendment of EO 9586: section 1 rewrote its numbered sections and section 2 amended EO 10717. EO 11515 (1970-03-13) substituted subsection 2(b) and struck all numbered sections other than 1 and 2, so the Board sections ended on that date while the Medal itself and the award provisions survive; EO 12014 (1977-10-19) abolished the Board, after those clauses had ended. The two amendment clauses (the section 1 lead-in and section 2(a)) are self-executing and ended on signing, 1963-02-22. Section 2(b) of the order (existing arrangements continue) is operative. The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; the held record contains no current-law text that names this order, so the claim rests on the absence of an ending in the bounded searches and in the held chain.
